cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and what you built after the change is still standing.
cells.act: give one thing and take one thing, in balance
cells.ask: Pick someone who helped carry this through. Give back what it really cost them, and take what they hand you back — one exchange, both ways, then done.
cells.core:
You're in the settled part. What you kept after the upheaval has stayed kept, and the form you built around it is doing its job. Weight lands on you and you keep your shape under it — flexible strength, not a stiff brace. Nothing is buckling. When this is working, you feel the load and adjust to it rather than locking against it.

What hasn't happened yet is the return. People were steady for you while the change was running, and you've been steady since. Pick one of them, give back what it actually cost them, and take what they offer in the same exchange. Both directions, then done. What got preserved was carried, not owned, and the exchange is what keeps it alive.
cells.sheetLine: What you saved is holding. Return the favour at its real size.
cells.verb: holding steady what change has already produced

cells.tense: You will be bracing before the next thing lands, holding weight that has not even shifted yet.
cells.act: let yourself be drawn before you choose
cells.ask: Once this week, go toward whatever is pulling at you for ten minutes before you decide anything about it — just stand near it and look.
cells.core:
Held well, this is standing at the load-bearing point and staying responsive — weight comes down, you feel it, you shift. What's happening instead is that the shifting has stopped. Your grip has gone past the thing it was holding, and you're braced ahead of anything having moved. The waiting itself has gone tight, and the arms are locked.

The loosening starts small. Let one thing pull at you before you've decided it's safe — follow it a little way, once this week, and see what it is up close. Stop holding the future long enough to be drawn by something in it.

cells.tense: You stood at the door after the change closed, and you have not moved from it.
cells.act: defend the direction you chose against the next push
cells.ask: Pick one choice you made during the change that you still stand behind, and keep that heading the next time something pushes against it — say it plainly, once.
cells.core:
Something ended, and you stayed at the doorway after it closed. What you carry, you carry from the threshold, and you haven't turned toward what got built. That part of you is doing its work — endurance is fine. It's direction that's gone quiet, and the weight you're bearing is partly the one you're still holding from before.

Endurance isn't what's empty here. Direction is. Take one choice you made back then that you still stand behind, and keep that heading the next time someone or some worry pushes against it. Say it plainly, once. The heading is what you take back, and it comes to you before the ground does.
cells.sheetLine: You're still at the door. The room is behind you.

cells.tense: You are here, pen in hand, already keeping things steady and not counting it as your doing.
cells.act: make the call and carry it through
cells.ask: Decide something about what you've been steadying for the group and carry it the same day — no explaining why, just the call and the follow-through.
cells.core:
You hold it steady, and you'd say it simply works that way. Since the change settled, you've been the beam others rest on, and it doesn't register as a decision you're making. The point where things would fall if you set them down reads to you as just the situation's shape.

It isn't only the shape — there's a hand in it, and it's yours. Take what you've been holding for the others, a plan or a standard or something that stays put, decide something about it, and carry it the same day to whoever needs to hear it. No explaining why. The structure keeps running, and this is your hand on it.

The sentence that serves me more than them is 'the death-grip is already underway' — it frames the person as already failing; I've cut it to plain observation of what the hands are doing.
